![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14055472/assets/ff3b9f52ed01d991d1fff18e78c494488b53703669b6bb326b5436a19c952a18.png)

Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}x\,dA,\,$
where $D$ is the region enclosed between the curves $3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=9$ and ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=9,$ as shown in the picture.
worked_solution:
Notice that $D$ is a type II region. Since $x\ge 0,$ we obtain the following equations in terms of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=9 & \,⟹\,x=\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}} \\ 3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=9 & \,⟹\,x=\sqrt{3-\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's determine the limits of integration.

- To determine the $y$-limits, we need to find the $y$-coordinates of the points at which the curves intersect. So, we set the following equation and solve it for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}} & =\sqrt{3-\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}} \\ 9-{y}^{2} & =3-\frac{{y}^{2}}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3}{y}^{2} & =6 \\ {y}^{2} & =9\end{aligned}
$$

So, since our region lies above the line the $x$-axis, the $y$-limits are 
$0\le y\le 3.$

- To determine the left and right functions, we draw a horizontal arrow from left to right through the region, as usual.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14055472/assets/91f377562a1e94218b7be886cd63638e8881b0c4fac231a810bb6bff3a1fe643.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\sqrt{3-\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}}\le x\le \sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}.
$$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
{∬}_{D}x\,dA={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{\sqrt{3-{y}^{2}/3}}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}x\,dx\,dy
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{\sqrt{3-{y}^{2}/3}}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}x\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{\sqrt{3-{y}^{2}/3}}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}x\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{\sqrt{3-{y}^{2}/3}}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{2}(9-{y}^{2}-(3-\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}))\,dy \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}(6-\frac{2}{3}{y}^{2})\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}(6-\frac{2}{3}{y}^{2})\,dy & =\frac{1}{2}{[6y-\frac{2}{9}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(18-6-0) \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$
